did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 25 opens with Bildad the Shuhite speaking, presenting his words as part of the ongoing debate between Job and his friends.
Did you know? Bildad describes God as one who rules and inspires awe, while also making peace in the heavens.
Did you know? Bildad emphasizes the vast number of God’s armies and the reach of his light, using a rhetorical question to express that no one is beyond its light.

Did you know? The questions “How then can a mortal be righteous before God?” and “How can one born of a woman be pure?” express Bildad’s view that a person cannot claim absolute righteousness before God.
Did you know? Even the moon and stars are described as not shining brightly enough or being pure enough in God’s sight, emphasizing his superiority over the heavenly lights.
Did you know? At the end of his speech, Bildad uses the images “maggot” and “worm” to emphasize humanity’s smallness and frailty before God.
